questions.question: Credit Rating agency ICRA is head-quartered in which of the following places?
questions.questionHtml: Credit Rating agency ICRA is head-quartered in which of the following places?
questions.solution: ICRA Limited (ICRA) is an Indian independent and professional investment information and credit rating agency. It was established in 1991, and was originally named Investment Information and Credit Rating Agency of India Limited (IICRA India). It was a joint-venture between Moody's and various Indian commercial banks and financial services companies. The company changed its name to ICRA Limited, and went public on 13 April 2007, with a listing on the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange. It is head-quartered in Gurgaon.

questions.question: Who was the founder of 'Hindustan Insurance Society'?
questions.questionHtml: Who was the founder of 'Hindustan Insurance Society'?
questions.solution:
The Oriental Life Insurance Company, the first company in India offering life insurance coverage, was established in Kolkata in 1818 by "Anita Bhavsar" and others. Its primary target market was the Europeans based in India, and it charged Indians heftier premiums. Surendranath Tagore had founded Hindustan Insurance Society, which later became Life Insurance Corporation.

Surendranath Tagore was a Bengali author, literary scholar, and translator. He is particularly noted for translating a number of works of Rabindranath Tagore to English. A member of the Tagore family of Calcutta, he was born to Satyendranath Tagore and Gyanodanandini Devi in Bombay in 1872. Surendranath is credited with establishing a number of Indian-owned banks and insurance companies through which he sought to encourage indigenous industries.

questions.question: 'Global Insurance Market Report' (GIMAR) is published by
questions.questionHtml: 'Global Insurance Market Report' (GIMAR) is published by
questions.solution:
The GIMAR assesses developments relevant to the (re)insurance industry and identifies and documents some main risks and vulnerabilities for the industry. It does so to promote awareness of these developments and risks among IAIS members, stakeholders and interested parties more generally. By providing a financial system-wide assessment of developments and risks, the GIMAR also plays an important role in the IAIS's new macroprudential policy and surveillance framework.

The International Association of Insurance Supervisors (IAIS) is a voluntary membership organization of insurance supervisors and regulators from more than 200 jurisdictions. The mission of the IAIS is to promote effective and globally consistent supervision of the insurance industry in order to develop and maintain fair, safe and stable insurance markets for the benefit and protection of policyholders and to contribute to global financial stability.

questions.question: What does 'CDR' stands for?
questions.questionHtml: What does 'CDR' stands for?
questions.solution: Corporate Debt Restructuring ("CDR") mechanism is a voluntary non statutory mechanism under which financial institutions and banks come together to restructure the debt of companies facing financial difficulties due to internal or external factors, in order to provide timely support to such companies.

questions.question: When was India adapted BASEL - 1 guidelines?
questions.questionHtml: When was India adapted BASEL - 1 guidelines?
questions.solution: In 1988, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) introduced capital measurement system called Basel capital accord, also called as Basel 1. It focused almost entirely on credit risk, It defined capital and structure of risk weights for banks. The minimum capital requirement was fixed at 8% of risk weighted assets (RWA). India adopted Basel 1 guidelines in 1999.

questions.question: Which among the following is the central banking institute in India?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following is the central banking institute in India?
questions.solution: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is India's central banking institution, which controls the monetary policy of the Indian rupee. It commenced its operations on 1 April 1935 during the British Rule in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. The original share capital was divided into shares of 100 each fully paid, which were initially owned entirely by private shareholders. Following India's independence on 15 August 1947, the RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949.

questions.question: What does 'R' stands for in 'LIBOR'?
questions.questionHtml: What does 'R' stands for in 'LIBOR'?
questions.solution: LIBOR or ICE LIBOR (previously BBA LIBOR) is a benchmark rate that some of the world's leading banks charge each other for short-term loans. It stands for Intercontinental Exchange London Interbank Offered Rate and serves as the first step to calculating interest rates on various loans throughout the world. LIBOR is administered by the ICE Benchmark Administration (IBA), and is based on five currencies: U.S. dollar (USD), Euro (EUR), pound sterling (GBP), Japanese yen (JPY) and Swiss franc (CHF), and serves seven different maturities: overnight, one week, and 1, 2, 3, 6 and 12 months. There are a total of 35 different LIBOR rates each business day. The most commonly quoted rate is the three-month U.S. dollar rate.

questions.question: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India was established in
questions.questionHtml: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India was established in
questions.solution: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) is the regulator for overseeing insolvency proceedings and entities like Insolvency Professional Agencies (IPA), Insolvency Professionals (IP) and Information Utilities (IU) in India. It was established on 1 October 2016 and given statutory powers through the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, which was passed by Lok Sabha on 5 May 2016. It covers Individuals, Companies, Limited Liability Partnerships and Partnership firms. The new code will speed up the resolution process for stressed assets in the country. It attempts to simplify the process of insolvency and bankruptcy proceedings. It handles the cases using two tribunals like NCLT(National company law tribunal) and Debt recovery tribunal.

questions.question: Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) is working under the supervision of
questions.questionHtml: Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) is working under the supervision of
questions.solution: The Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) was an agency of the government of India, part of the Department of Financial Services of the Ministry of Finance. Its objective is to determine sickness of industrial companies and to assist in reviving those that may be viable and shutting down the others. But from 1 December 2016, by an official notification, Government of India dissolved it and all proceedings to be referred to the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) and National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) as per provisions of Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.

questions.question: Which among the following is the legal basis for setting up of Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs) in India?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following is the legal basis for setting up of Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs) in India?

options.text: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act 2002
options.html: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act 2002

questions.solution: The Securitization and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest (SARFAESI) Act, 2002; enacted in December 2002 provides the legal basis for the setting up ARCs in India. Section 2 (1) of the Act explains the meaning of Asset Securitization. Similarly, ARCs are also elaborated under Section 3 of the of the Act. The SARFAESI Act helps reconstruction of bad assets without the intervention of courts. Since then, large number of ARCs were formed and were registered with the RBI which has got the power to regulate the ARCs.

questions.question: What does 'T' stands for in 'UTR Number'?
questions.questionHtml: What does 'T' stands for in 'UTR Number'?
questions.solution: The term UTR No. means Unique Transaction Reference Number and it is generally used in association with NEFT transactions done through bank. For every successful NEFT transaction, your Bank will provide a UTR number (Unique Transaction Reference No.). For example, if you do the a NEFT transaction with a branch of Union Bank of India, the Union Bank of India will provide the UTR No. to you which can be used to track the transaction later. So, UTR number is a unique code for identifying the NEFT transaction.

questions.question: Federal Reserve System is the central banking system of which of the following countries?
questions.questionHtml: Federal Reserve System is the central banking system of which of the following countries?
questions.solution: The Federal Reserve System (also known as the Federal Reserve or simply the Fed) is the central banking system of the United States. It was created on December 23, 1913, with the enactment of the Federal Reserve Act, after a series of financial panics (particularly the panic of 1907) led to the desire for central control of the monetary system in order to alleviate financial crises. Over the years, events such as the Great Depression in the 1930s and the Great Recession during the 2000s, have led to the expansion of the roles and responsibilities of the Federal Reserve System.

questions.question: Which among the following provides the credit risk insurance covers to exporters against loss in export of goods and services?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following provides the credit risk insurance covers to exporters against loss in export of goods and services?
questions.solution:
The ECGC Limited (Formerly Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Ltd) is a company wholly owned by the Government of India based in Mumbai, Maharashtra.

Functions:

• Provides a range of credit risk insurance covers to exporters against loss in export of goods and services as well.

• Offers guarantees to banks and financial institutions to enable exporters to obtain better facilities from them.

questions.question: Short term interest bearing loans extended to government by RBI is referred to as _______?

questions.solution: The RBI as the banker to the State Governments provides financial accommodation to the States banking with it through agreement to tide over temporary mismatches in the cash flow of their receipts and payments under Ways and Means Advances. It is a short-term interest-bearing advance extended by RBI.

questions.question: Microinsurance was first adopted in India by IRDAI in which year?
questions.questionHtml: Microinsurance was first adopted in India by IRDAI in which year?
questions.solution: Micro insurance was formally adopted through the Microinsurance Regulations Act in 2005 by IRDAI. It is a special category of insurance policy to promote insurance coverage among economically vulnerable sections of society. Micro- insurance business is done through the following intermediaries: Non-Government Organisations Self-Help Groups Micro-Finance Institutions.

questions.question: Which among the following bonus is offered to policyholders as a recognition for maintaining the policy till the maturity period?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following bonus is offered to policyholders as a recognition for maintaining the policy till the maturity period?
questions.solution: Persistency Bonus is also referred to as terminal bonus. It is paid once, at the time of maturity of the policy. It is a sort of loyalty bonus given to a policyholder for maintaining the policy till maturity. Its value is not guaranteed and will be disclosed only at the time of policy maturity. This bonus will not be payable on policies which have acquired paid-up value or have been surrendered.

questions.question: Which among the following is a part of RBI's Liquid Adjustment Facility?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following is a part of RBI's Liquid Adjustment Facility?
questions.solution: Liquidity adjustment facility (LAF) is a monetary policy to which allows banks borrow money through repurchase agreements, which are Repo rate and Reverse Repo Rate from the central banks. Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) was introduced by the RBI in June 2000 to control monetary policy.

questions.question: The reduced amount of sum assured paid by the insurer in case of discontinuation of payment of premium is referred to as which among the following?
questions.questionHtml: The reduced amount of sum assured paid by the insurer in case of discontinuation of payment of premium is referred to as which among the following?
questions.solution: After premiums are paid for a certain defined period or beyond and if subsequent premiums are not paid, the sum assured is reduced to a proportionate sum, which bears the same ratio to the full sum assured as the number of premiums actually paid bears to the total number originally stipulated in the policy. This is referred to as Paid up Value.

questions.question: In insurance sector, the term "Penetration Rate" refers to which of the following?
questions.questionHtml: In insurance sector, the term "Penetration Rate" refers to which of the following?

options.text: Ratio of premium to total population
options.html: Ratio of premium to total population

options.text: Ratio of life insurance to non-life insurance policy subscription
options.html: Ratio of life insurance to non-life insurance policy subscription

options.text: Ratio of insurance companies to total population
options.html: Ratio of insurance companies to total population

options.text: Ratio of insured to un-insured population.
options.html: Ratio of insured to un-insured population.

questions.solution: Penetration rate indicates the level of development of insurance sector in a country. Penetration rate is measured as the ratio of premium underwritten in a particular year to the GDP. This includes both life insurance and non-life insurance. As per the IRDA data, Insurance penetration of India i.e. Premium collected by Indian insurers was 3.44% of GDP in FY 2015-16 and this is expected to go beyond 4% in the current and upcoming financial year.

questions.question: Insurance Awareness Day is observed on ________?
questions.questionHtml: Insurance Awareness Day is observed on ________?
questions.solution: IRDAI's 'Formation Day' is celebrated as Insurance Awareness Day on 19th April every year. Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDA) set up as autonomous body under the IRDA Act, 1999, with the mission to protect the interests of policyholders, to regulate, promote and ensure orderly growth of the insurance industry and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. On 19th April 2000 IRDA formally came into existence.

questions.question: The Reinstatement Value method is related to which among the following type of insurances?
questions.questionHtml: The Reinstatement Value method is related to which among the following type of insurances?
questions.solution: The Reinstatement Value Method (RIV), is used in property insurance to fix the sum insured. In the RIV method, the Insurance Co. will pay the cost of replacement subject to ceiling of S.I. Under this method, no depreciation is levied. One condition is that the damaged asset should be repaired / replaced in order to get the claim. RIV method is allowed only for FIXED ASSETS and not for other assets like stocks and stocks in process.
